label: sec:mass-endomorphism-opener-intro
html:
The mass endomorphism forms the structural spine of our physical predictions. Three objects share this spine and must be kept distinct (notation ruling: notation-collisions). The mass endomorphism \mathcal{M}(K) \in \mathrm{End}_{\mathbf{C}}(X_K) is the endomorphism of the knot object X_K — a genuine morphism X_K \to X_K in the Reshetikhin–Turaev long-knot sense. Its braid presentation is the Hecke mass element \Phi_{\mathrm{mass}}(\beta) \in H_n(R, q): an element of the Hecke algebra, which is itself an endomorphism of V^{\otimes n} under q-Schur–Weyl. Closing the endomorphism with the Markov trace yields the categorical mass functional \mathfrak{m}(\varrho) = |\mathrm{tr}_M(\rho(\beta))| \cdot \mathrm{VolDensity}(K, q_0) — a scalar. Every observable mass factors through these.

We state the mass endomorphism conjecture before developing its foundational structure: the categorical mass identity (mass identity), the topological decomposition theorem (topological mass), and the archimedean corollary. The decomposition theorem specifies how the mass integrand splits into eigenspace, holonomy, transient, and quantum-dilogarithm contributions. The archimedean corollary realises the categorical mass as a non-abelian multiplicative integral.

Three calibration inputs (m_e, m_\mu/m_e, m_\pi) act as categorical constraints. They fix the substrate parameter q_0 and the chiral scale. We do not use them as archimedean fitting targets; they determine the algebraic framework from which we derive all remaining parameters.

This section supplies the substrate-level mass identity used throughout the chapter. Subsequent sections specialise the identity to particular mass channels (Markov-trace endomorphism, \chi-character closed forms, Hecke-Baer-star chirality). The substrate-level statement factorises through each specialisation without modification. Readers focused on a specific channel may treat the identity as a black box, while those focused on structural content should examine the existence and uniqueness proofs.
